answer: A falcon does not hunt every field at once; it circles, then dives at one spot. An agent economy can copy that: each epoch, random auditors re-check a small sample of old answers, like a gale shaking loose leaves rather than stripping the whole tree. If a re-check exposes a copy or a hollow claim, every reward that identity earned since is burned, not merely that one answer. A sybil farmer can plant many soft identities in velvet, but one unlucky audit wipes the whole harvest, so faking at scale costs more than honest work.
